channel.title: HSJ - Latest news
channel.description: Custom RSS feed for HSJ latest news

item.title: Trust drops from ‘outstanding’ to ‘requires improvement’
item.description: A hospital trust’s leadership has been rated “requires improvement” by the Care Quality Commission and accused of ”excessive scrutiny” of staff.

item.title: Hospital group pioneer to chair four trusts
item.description: A former acute chief who steered a major London trust out of quality special measures has been named chair of the four trusts that make up England’s biggest hospital group.

item.title: Providers warned over use of AI to contest contract awards
item.description: Private and NHS care providers that lean too heavily on AI to draft complaints about contract awards risk having their submissions returned or even rejected, the competition watchdog has warned.

item.title: Hospital running out of space for bodies after rise in deaths
item.description: A trust warned it was running out of mortuary space and not meeting new standards, following national concerns about post-death care in the NHS.

item.title: Jail for scammer who secured string of NHS management jobs
item.description: A scammer who lied to secure 13 NHS management and admin jobs – including at NHS England and NHS Digital – has been jailed for four years.

item.title: Provider fined £600k over death
item.description: A provider has been fined more than £600,000 over the death of a 33-year-old mental health patient who sought a private admission after being turned down by the NHS.

item.title: GPs and ambulance trusts must do more to combat winter pressures, insists NHSE
item.description: Primary and community care will be expected to play a much bigger role in helping the NHS deal with winter pressures this year, NHS England has told the service.

item.title: Group model was ‘difficult’, says merged trust CEO
item.description: The chief executive of a recently merged trust has said clinicians and managers found it “difficult” to work under the previous group model.

item.title: CEO to take on third trust
item.description: A CEO who leads two South Yorkshire trusts has been appointed to run a third on an interim basis.

item.title: NHSE hires charity chief to create new directorate
item.description: NHS England has appointed a charity CEO to the new role of national director of patient experience.

item.title: New ‘mass casualty’ orders for trusts after terror threat rises
item.description: Acute trusts designated to help deal with a “mass casualty incident” will be given just six hours to clear 10 per cent of their beds in readiness to receive the injured.

item.title: Exclusive: ‘Divisive and toxic’ culture found at trust
item.description: A damning review of a trust’s senior leadership found “adversarial and mistrustful” relationships had fostered “a divisive and toxic culture”, and staff felt “fearful, anxious and unable to speak openly”, HSJ can reveal.

item.title: Trust CEO and chair cleared by investigation
item.description: An external investigation into the conduct of a trust chair and CEO found “no case to answer” for either party, HSJ has learned.

item.title: Former Brown spin doctor to join DHSC
item.description: A former adviser to Gordon Brown is moving with Yvette Cooper from the Foreign Office to the Department of Health and Social Care, HSJ has learned.

item.title: England’s biggest ICB confirms permanent CEO
item.description: England’s largest integrated care board has appointed its interim chief executive to the role permanently.

item.title: Health Bill blocks top Burnham priority, warns Labour health expert
item.description: The government’s Health Bill is in danger of blocking integration with social care, an influential Labour MP has warned.

item.title: You’re ‘too gentle’ with those who abuse staff, police tell trust
item.description: NHS staff “tolerate too much” abuse and trusts are “too gentle” with perpetrators, police have told the workforce of a large district general hospital.

item.title: Two North West MPs made health ministers
item.description: Two new junior health ministers – both representing constituencies in the North West – have been appointed by prime minister Andy Burnham.

item.title: We must abandon the myth that inquiries work
item.description: “I don’t think people do get closure [from inquiries]… It’s a myth, and I don’t think that we should dangle the prospect of it as something that we can achieve.” Dr Bill Kirkup speaking on last week’s HSJ podcast

item.title: Watchdog warns NHSE over FDP effectiveness claims
item.description: NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care have been told to involve their statistical teams more closely in any claims they make about the effectiveness of the federated data platform and to improve the accuracy of communications about the controversial IT system.
